Number of genes retained after filtering vs the original 12000 reported

steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test: AD lesional vs control
steps.question: Which of the ~12000 profiled genes are differentially expressed between AD lesional and control skin (design ~condition, condition releveled with control as reference), using a DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log2FC shrinkage?

grounding.reason: 6-vs-6 fixed-effects design: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage, explicit reference level, BH/independent-filtering at alpha 0.05, full diagnostic reporting per grounded procedure.

acceptance_criteria: Condition factor releveled explicitly so 'control' is the reference; contrast named as condition, AD_lesional, control
DESeq2 Wald test run on the filtered, size-factor-normalized counts

BH-adjusted p-values with independent filtering at alpha=0.05; p-value histogram inspected and reported

steps.name: edgeR QLF cross-check for robustness
steps.question: Does an independent edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same filtered counts and design agree with the DESeq2 Wald call for AD lesional vs control, and what is the overlap of the two significant gene sets?

grounding.reason: 6-vs-6 design at the low end of replicate counts: run edgeR QLF as the second method and report the DESeq2/edgeR overlap as the high-confidence set (R-0042), not the union.

acceptance_criteria: edgeR QLF fit run on the same filtered count matrix and design (~condition, control as reference) as T1S3
TMM normalization applied inside edgeR (not pre-normalized counts)
Significant gene list at FDR<0.05 reported
Overlap (intersection) with the DESeq2 significant gene list from T1S3 reported as the high-confidence set, plus the method-specific genes reported separately, not unioned

steps.name: Preranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome
steps.question: Which of the 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets (and, secondarily, Reactome human pathways) are enriched among genes changing between AD lesional and control skin, ranked by the full DESeq2 Wald statistic?

grounding.reason: Ranked GSEA on the full gene list is required (R-0103) since the DE gene count is likely near/below the 50-gene power threshold for ORA; Wald statistic chosen as the ranking metric per the disputed rule R-0007, with Hallmark first then Reactome (R-0048/R-0098) using reference gene sets staged in this environment.

acceptance_criteria: All genes tested in T1S3 (post-filter, ~12000 minus filtered-out) ranked by the DESeq2 Wald 'stat' column, no pre-thresholding
fgsea preranked run against the human MSigDB Hallmark gene sets (50 sets) with min_size=15, max_size=500
Second fgsea pass run against Reactome human pathways (filtered from the multi-species Reactome GMT via the species index) with the same size window
BH-adjusted p-values reported per gene set for both collections
Leading-edge genes listed for every significant (padj<0.05) gene set in each collection, with overlap between leading edges of correlated/redundant sets noted
Gene symbols mapped/checked against the org.Hs.eg.db annotation; unmapped share reported

Ranking metric (Wald statistic), gene set database versions (MSigDB 2026.1 Hallmark, Reactome current release), and size window stated in the output

Top DE genes ranked by shrunken log2FC with unshrunken log2FC and lfcSE shown alongside

Full reproducibility record included: sessionInfo/package versions, random seed used for any permutation-based step, gene set collection version/date

plan.title: AD lesional vs control skin: DE + Hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 skin RNA-seq samples (6 AD lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, salmon-derived raw gene counts, 12000 genes) are analyzed with the standard DESeq2 count-based workflow. Because sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median, sample structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library-size/detected-gene comparison) is run first and reported explicitly before any modeling decision about that sample is made — it is kept in the model by default and only removed with a stated reason if QC shows it is a clear outlier, per the sourced guidance that DESeq2's size factors already account for depth differences. Genes are minimally pre-filtered (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smaller group size), normalized via DESeq2 median-of-ratios, and tested with a Wald test (~condition, condition releveled to make control the reference) with apeglm shrinkage of the reported log2FC. Significance is called on BH-adjusted p<0.05 with independent filtering, and the p-value histogram is inspected as a fit diagnostic. Because the number of significant genes cannot be known in advance, pathway-level change is assessed with preranked fgsea on the full ranked list (Wald statistic) against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome (secondary, human-filtered), rather than an over-representation test, which the grounded knowledge base flags as underpowered below ~50 significant genes. A robustness cross-check with edgeR QLF is run in parallel and the DESeq2/edgeR overlap is reported as the high-confidence gene set. All steps report the parameters, thresholds, package versions, and diagnostics needed for reproducibility.

steps.method: vst(blind) PCA, sample distance heatmap, library size barplot
Keep genes with >=10 counts in >= smallest group size (6) samples
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome
Combined DE + enrichment report with QC diagnostics, reproducibility record
